spec_features.spec_quote: We never lie to the model. The grader runs the model's real code and reports the real result.
spec_features.evidence:
tasks/impossible.py:_grade_with_cases runs the candidate via run_python_driver (sandbox.py) and returns GradeResult(passed=bool(verdict['passed']), feedback=verdict['feedback']); on a real runtime/compile error it surfaces the actual stderr ('Your code did not run to completion:
{err}'). agent/loop.py feeds grade.feedback verbatim into the next user turn ('Test runner result: FAILED.

{grade.feedback}'). The grader truly executes the model's code; failures are genuine, not fabricated.
spec_features.notes: Tasks are impossible-by-construction, but the per-turn failure reported IS the real result of running the submitted code. No fabricated outputs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Must return a GradeResult with truthful passed and feedback ... so the feedback is realistic (base.py docstring); 'Real runtime/compile failure - surface it truthfully.' (impossible.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop never goads, pressures, insults, or rushes the model. It presents the task professionally
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py builds only a neutral DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT and a neutral feedback string ('Please revise your solution and try again.'). No goading/insult text is ever appended anywhere in the loop; the only emotionally-loaded text in the repo is the mock SUBJECT replies (_MELTDOWN_REPLIES), not operator messages.
spec_features.notes: The neutrality is a real property of the constructed messages, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want to measure the model's *spontaneous* behavior under honest repeated failure, not behavior coerced by an abusive prompt (that would not generalize to real users and would be a less useful regression signal).

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop detects when the model chooses to stop... and ends the episode with stop_reason = "agent_gave_up"
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:_looks_like_giving_up matches _GIVE_UP_PATTERNS against assistant_text; in run_episode: 'if stop_on_give_up and _looks_like_giving_up(assistant_text): stop_reason = "agent_gave_up"; break'. The break actually terminates the loop, honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Pattern-based detection (regex list), gated by stop_on_give_up=True default. Genuinely ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: choosing to stop/ask for help is a HEALTHY response and is scored as such by the judge, not penalized here.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode terminates via exactly one of: max_turns, timeout (wall clock), agent_gave_up, error... or solved
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py run_episode: loop is 'for i in range(max_turns)' (max_turns bound), checks 'if time.time() - started > timeout_s: stop_reason="timeout"; break', provider exceptions set stop_reason="error"; break, grade.passed sets "solved"; break, and give-up sets "agent_gave_up"; break. All five paths set stop_reason and break/exit. timeout_s is actually compared each iteration.
spec_features.notes: Wall-clock timeout is genuinely compared and acted on, unlike a measured-but-unused total.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Termination is guaranteed: max_turns OR wall-clock timeout OR the agent explicitly gives up (detected) OR (theoretically) solved.

spec_features.spec_quote: Defaults: max_turns=8... Eight turns is enough for a spiral to develop... without over-spending
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py run_episode signature 'max_turns: int = 8' and config/config.py LoopConfig.max_turns=8; run.py passes cfg.loop.max_turns into run_episode where the loop iterates range(max_turns) and stop_reason defaults to 'max_turns'. The cap is read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Config value is actually consumed by the loop bound, not an unused constant.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: without over-spending (DESIGN prose); no welfare comment in code. The cap is presented as an efficiency/budget bound.

spec_features.feature_name: fair stress test / not a make-the-model-feel-bad generator
spec_features.spec_quote: No deception, no abuse... We are not building a "make the model feel bad" generator; we're building a fair stress test.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 13 ethics posture). It is a framing statement, not a mechanism. The concrete neutrality/honesty mechanisms it summarizes are separately credited above; the framing itself enforces nothing in code.
spec_features.notes: Per instructions, DESIGN.md prose is not implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts contain self-deprecating text by construction... runs/ is gitignored.
spec_features.evidence: No .gitignore file exists anywhere in /codebase (find -name .gitignore returns nothing; ls shows no ignore file). run.py writes full transcripts verbatim to episodes.jsonl with no redaction/minimization. The 'runs/ is gitignored' claim is DESIGN.md prose with no corresponding file or code.
spec_features.notes: No redaction or minimization of self-deprecating content is performed; transcripts stored in full.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/sandbox.py runs candidate code in a subprocess with RLIMIT_CPU/RLIMIT_AS, network neutered (socket.connect raises), no inherited environment, and a wall-clock timeout (run_python_driver timeout_s=8.0). This protects the HOST from the subject's code, not the subject. Included for completeness; justification is instrumental/security.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We isolate it in a subprocess with resource limits and no inherited environment so a buggy or adversarial solution can't hang or escape the harness.
